task: CI/CD Pipeline Setup and Deployment Configuration

stack.frontend: React + Vite, located in root /src, built with 'npm run build' outputting to /dist
stack.backend: Node.js + Express + Socket.io + Ably, located in /backend, entry point is backend/server.js
stack.realtime: Socket.io and Ably — requires persistent process, NOT serverless
stack.auth: JWT in HTTP-only cookies — requires SameSite=None + Secure=true in production cross-domain setup

deployment_targets.frontend: Vercel — Git integration, automatic preview deployments per PR, Vite-optimized
deployment_targets.backend: Railway — persistent Node.js process, WebSocket support, environment variable management

context.repository: GitHub — single monorepo with frontend in root and backend in /backend folder

phase_1_project_preparation.description: Prepare the codebase for CI/CD and cross-domain production deployment before writing any pipeline config

tasks.name: Environment Variable Audit
steps: Create a .env.example file in root listing all required frontend env vars: VITE_API_URL, VITE_ABLY_KEY, VITE_SOCKET_URL

Create a .env.example file in /backend listing all required backend env vars: MONGODB_URI, JWT_SECRET, ABLY_API_KEY, EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_PORT, EMAIL_USER, EMAIL_PASS, ADMIN_EMAIL, CLIENT_URL, NODE_ENV, PORT
Ensure .env and .env.local are in .gitignore — never commit secrets
Replace all hardcoded localhost URLs in frontend with import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL
Replace all hardcoded localhost URLs in backend with process.env.CLIENT_URL for CORS

tasks.name: Cross-Domain Cookie Fix
steps: In backend/server.js, update the cookie settings for JWT to: { httpOnly: true, secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production', sameSite: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 'none' : 'lax' }
Update CORS configuration to use process.env.CLIENT_URL as the allowed origin, with credentials: true
In frontend, ensure all fetch/axios calls include credentials: 'include' or withCredentials: true

tasks.name: Socket.io Production Config
steps: In frontend socket initialization, set transports: ['websocket'] to avoid polling fallback issues in production
In backend socket.io setup, confirm cors origin uses process.env.CLIENT_URL
Set the socket server URL in frontend using import.meta.env.VITE_SOCKET_URL

tasks.name: Add Test Infrastructure
steps: Install Vitest and @testing-library/react in root for frontend tests: npm install -D vitest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom jsdom
Install Jest and supertest in /backend for API tests: npm install -D jest supertest mongodb-memory-server
Add test scripts to both package.json files: 'test': 'vitest run' (frontend) and 'test': 'jest' (backend)

Create at minimum 3 backend test files: backend/tests/auth.test.js (register/login routes), backend/tests/admin.test.js (protected route auth check), backend/tests/messages.test.js (message creation and fetch)
Create at minimum 2 frontend test files: src/tests/App.test.jsx (renders without crash), src/tests/auth.test.jsx (login form renders and submits)
Use mongodb-memory-server in backend tests to avoid needing a real MongoDB connection in CI

tasks.name: Add Linting Config
steps: Ensure ESLint is configured in root with an .eslintrc or eslint.config.js for the React frontend
Add ESLint to /backend with Node.js rules
Add lint scripts: 'lint': 'eslint src --ext .js,.jsx' in frontend and 'lint': 'eslint . --ext .js' in backend
Fix any existing lint errors before proceeding

tasks.name: Vercel Configuration File
steps: Create vercel.json in the project root with the following config:
{ 'buildCommand': 'npm run build', 'outputDirectory': 'dist', 'framework': 'vite', 'rewrites': [{ 'source': '/(.*)', 'destination': '/index.html' }] }
This ensures React Router client-side routing works correctly on Vercel

tasks.name: Railway Configuration File
steps: Create a Procfile or railway.toml in /backend
railway.toml content: [build] builder = 'NIXPACKS' [deploy] startCommand = 'node server.js' healthcheckPath = '/api/health' restartPolicyType = 'ON_FAILURE'
Add a health check endpoint in backend/server.js: app.get('/api/health', (req, res) => res.json({ status: 'ok', timestamp: new Date() }))
Ensure backend/package.json has 'start': 'node server.js' and 'engines': { 'node': '>=18.0.0' }

phase_2_github_actions_ci_pipeline.description: Create the CI workflow that runs on every push and pull request to validate code integrity

steps: Checkout code
Setup Node.js 20
Cache node_modules for /backend
Run: cd backend && npm install
Run: cd backend && npm run lint
Run: cd backend && npm test (uses mongodb-memory-server, no external DB needed)
Checkout code
Setup Node.js 20
Cache node_modules for root
Run: npm install
Run: npm run lint
Run: npm test
Run: npm run build (ensures Vite build succeeds — catches import errors, missing env types, etc.)
Checkout code
Setup Node.js 20
Run: npm audit --audit-level=high in root
Run: cd backend && npm audit --audit-level=high
Use 'continue-on-error: false' to fail the pipeline on high/critical vulnerabilities

phase_3_github_actions_cd_pipeline.description: Create the CD workflow that deploys to Vercel and Railway only when CI passes on the main branch

workflow_spec.name: CD — Deploy to Vercel and Railway
triggers: condition: CI workflow must pass first (use needs or workflow_run)

steps: Checkout code
Setup Node.js 20
Run: npm install
Install Vercel CLI: npm install -g vercel
Run: vercel pull --yes --environment=production --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
Run: vercel build --prod --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
Run: vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
github_secrets_required: VERCEL_TOKEN — from Vercel dashboard under Account Settings > Tokens
VERCEL_ORG_ID — from .vercel/project.json after first vercel link
VERCEL_PROJECT_ID — from .vercel/project.json after first vercel link

steps: Checkout code
Install Railway CLI: npm install -g @railway/cli
Run: railway up --service kickstream-backend --detach (deploys /backend directory)
Railway auto-detects Node.js and uses the start command from package.json or railway.toml
github_secrets_required: RAILWAY_TOKEN — from Railway dashboard under Account Settings > Tokens
RAILWAY_SERVICE_ID — the service ID from Railway project dashboard
jobs.alternative: Instead of CLI, use Railway's built-in GitHub integration (connect repo in Railway dashboard and set root directory to /backend) — this is simpler and removes the need for RAILWAY_TOKEN in GitHub secrets. Railway will auto-deploy on push to main. Recommend this approach for simplicity.

phase_4_environment_variable_setup.description: Configure all environment variables in each deployment platform

items.name: Preview Deployments for PRs
items.description: Vercel automatically creates preview URLs for every PR. Add a GitHub Actions comment bot that posts the preview URL as a PR comment for easy review.

items.name: Dependabot
items.description: Create .github/dependabot.yml to auto-create PRs for outdated npm dependencies weekly. Config: { version: 2, updates: [{ package-ecosystem: 'npm', directory: '/', schedule: { interval: 'weekly' } }, { package-ecosystem: 'npm', directory: '/backend', schedule: { interval: 'weekly' } }] }

items.name: Branch Protection Rules
items.description: In GitHub repo Settings > Branches, protect the main branch: require CI to pass before merge, require at least 1 PR review, disallow direct pushes to main.

items.name: Railway Staging Environment
items.description: Create a second Railway service connected to a 'dev' branch for staging deployments before promoting to production.

implementation_order: 1. Phase 1: Prepare codebase (env vars, cookie fix, CORS, Socket.io config, tests, vercel.json, railway.toml)
2. Phase 4: Set up all environment variables in Vercel and Railway dashboards first
3. Phase 2: Create and commit .github/workflows/ci.yml — test it triggers correctly on a test branch push
4. Phase 3: Create and commit .github/workflows/deploy.yml — verify first deploy succeeds
5. Phase 5: Add branch protection, Dependabot, and preview URL comment bot
success_criteria: Pushing to any branch triggers CI: lint, test, and build all pass
A failing test or lint error blocks the pipeline and prevents merge
Merging to main automatically deploys frontend to Vercel and backend to Railway
The live app at the Vercel URL connects correctly to the Railway backend via HTTPS
Socket.io real-time features (chat, notifications) work in production
JWT cookie auth works cross-domain in production
Health check endpoint /api/health returns 200 on Railway
npm audit reports no high or critical vulnerabilities
